title: a scene of several actors with lighting and a volume, placed and verified
proves: describe a scene as desired state, place it in one call, read it back independently, and save the level

editor.reason: install gate refused; no editor was contacted

install_gate.reason: Set MCP_UNREAL_PROJECT_ROOT to the test project root

steps.label: 1. find the PlayerStart the trigger volume must stay away from
steps.detail: install gate refused; no editor was contacted

steps.label: primitive puerts_scene_batch is NOT usable
steps.detail: PORT: actor_spawn (MCP_ENABLE_LEGACY_HTTP=1) + batch_spawn (MCP_ENABLE_LEGACY_HTTP=1) + actor_organize (MCP_ENABLE_LEGACY_HTTP=1) already does this, with no native front
steps.why: puerts_spawn_actor takes a class path and nothing else: it cannot label an actor, cannot scale it, cannot file it in an outliner folder, cannot set a volume's extent and cannot batch. Seven separate spawns with no way to name what they produced is not a scene-authoring primitive

steps.label: 2. place the whole courtyard in one desired-state call
primitive puerts_scene_inspect is NOT usable
steps.detail: PORT: level_actors (MCP_ENABLE_LEGACY_HTTP=1) + level_outliner (MCP_ENABLE_LEGACY_HTTP=1) already does this, with no native front
steps.why: puerts_find_actors returns names and classes only. It reports no transform, no folder, no bounds and no structure hash, so there is no way to verify a placement without one

steps.label: 3. read the level back with the independent scene inspector
